title: Tech Note: Included Lists with 4D View
featured_technology: 4D View area used as a 'subform-type' area

historical_commentary.text: This note covers using a 4D View area (the spreadsheet-like plug-in available since 4D v6.8) as an alternative to a true subform, focusing specifically on 'included lists' within that View area. The 4D View plug-in was discontinued years ago, its spreadsheet/grid capabilities superseded first by the built-in List Box object and much later by the separate 4D View Pro product (2018), so the specific technique of using a 4D View area as a subform substitute is now obsolete, though the underlying idea of embedding a grid-like area for tabular subordinate data persists conceptually in today's List Box-based forms.
related_updates: The original 4D View plug-in has been discontinued and replaced conceptually by 4D's built-in List Box form object
4D View Pro (introduced 2018) is a separate, modern spreadsheet component unrelated to the legacy 4D View plug-in described here
Modern 4D forms handle list/subform-style tabular data through native List Box objects or Project Mode form objects rather than embedding a 4D View area
